description: Price pick lines (player prop lines from a pick'em or sportsbook app) against StatHead's week projections: for each player + stat + line, the week's projected stat, the simulation median, the lean (over / under), P(lean), the edge against the payout's break-even (1 / multiplier) and the expected value per unit. The raw share of 20,000 draws of the player's week stat line past the line (pRaw; pOver via fields) comes from the same stat-line simulation that makes the confidence bands; P(lean) is that share CALIBRATED, 0.5 + 0.5 x (raw - 0.5) capped at 62%, because on a proxy back test (weeks 1-6 of 2026, 2,429 lines set at an external projection's number) the raw share ranked outcomes correctly (hit rate rose monotonically with it) but overstated them by about half (62% hit where it said 81%, 57% where it said 60%), and on weeks 1-7 (2,786 leans) the hit rate stopped rising at about 62% (leans the shrink put at 71-76% hit 58%); leans clearing the break-even hit 58.6%, nearly all of it on unders, since single games are right-skewed. Stats: recYds, rushYds, passYds, rec, tgt, rushAtt, passTD, rushRecYds (rush + rec yards), passRushYds, anyTD (rush + rec TDs). The lines and payouts are the caller's inputs and are echoed back; nothing else third-party is involved. GUARDRAILS: a row is flagged, and should not be trusted on the number alone, when the player or a position-mate is Questionable / Doubtful / Out for the week (the line is conditional on playing; the book knows more about the game-time call), when the role update moved his line 15%+ (role:x), when a projected volume is thin (under 2 targets / 4 carries / 10 attempts), or when his game has already started. A 1.78x payout needs 56.2% to break even, 1.87x 53.5%: edge is P(lean) minus that, so a 51% lean is not a pick. Lines are priced at the if-he-plays line; a player with no row in the weekly feed has no price (and a teammate missing from the feed means the pool spreads his volume to the room — check the depth chart). To keep a track record, record priced lines with scripts/price-lines.py --record in the repo; the weekly scorer grades them and the daily report shows hit rate and calibration by confidence. See also: get_metadata for season coverage, valid enums, and analytic caveats.

lines.description: Semicolon-separated lines, each 'Player stat number [@mult]' (e.g. 'Germie Bernard recYds 54.5 @1.78; Jaylin Noel rec yds 27.5; Josh Allen pass yds 260.5'). Aliases like 'rec yds', 'receiving yards', 'rush+rec yds', 'receptions' are accepted.

mult.description: Payout per leg for lines that give none (default 1.78)

name: price_lines
